data.gender_notes: Aadam is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Aadam (Peaceful) was the first man created by Allah. According to Islamic belief, he was created from clay and given the soul by Allah. Aadam is considered the father of humanity and is mentioned in the Quran several times. The name Aadam carries the meaning “First man created by Allah” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Aadam usually hope their child will grow to embody first man created by allah and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the beginning of life and the concept of creation.
data.etymology: Aadam belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “First man created by Allah.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Aadam total 2, giving a life-path number of 2. Number 2 is linked with Moon and with the qualities of harmony, sensitivity and partnership.

Moreover, Aadam's fall from grace, together with Hawwa, etched a lesson on temptation and humility for generations to come. Overall, Aadam's name carries a powerful reminder of our humble beginnings and the origin of mankind.
